scope: All 32 Go-port milestone chunks, all 17 related PRs including the superseded closed PR and stabilization PR, cumulative Go source, tests, conformance, architecture, dependencies, CI, release and Python migration boundaries.
limits: This is an audit of delivered code and planned work, not a claim that unimplemented chunks or unpublished upstream modules have been tested. Historical PR check results apply to their recorded heads. New fixes require new CI.

issues.title: Go port 00: Record the Go port and cutover decision in an ADR
issues.evidence: ADR 0047 and its index. PR #584 merged into go-cutover.

acceptance.criterion: An accepted ADR records each point above.
acceptance.evidence: ADR 0047 accepted.

acceptance.criterion: The ADR index shows the new ADR and the new status of each ADR that it supersedes or amends.
acceptance.evidence: ADR index records amendments and supersessions.

acceptance.criterion: No code changes.
acceptance.evidence: PR #584 changes only the ADR and index.

issues.title: Go port 01: List the RAES operations that env-packs uses and call them through one Go interface
issues.evidence: Interface declarations and symbol map exist. No adapter or operation contract tests exist. The current dev API has also moved; refresh the map on synchronization. Seven operation families lack a named upstream delivery issue.

acceptance.criterion: The interface package declares every operation in the table and the operations that chunk 27 needs.
acceptance.evidence: Content checks need custom backend-manifest planning, realization concern descriptors, compiled document access and has_required_observation_support. Existing interfaces do not represent all of these.

acceptance.criterion: The map covers all 72 symbols.
acceptance.evidence: The 78-symbol map covers the old application tree, not current dev or all retained content tests.

acceptance.criterion: A document in `docs/development/` lists the RAES issue that delivers each operation, or states that none exists.
acceptance.evidence: Operations page maps application groups and lists seven upstream gaps; retained content-test operations need the same mapping.

acceptance.criterion: Only the adapter imports the RAES Go module, and the architecture check (chunk 04) enforces this.
acceptance.evidence: raes-through-adapter rejects RAES imports everywhere until an adapter exception is designed.

acceptance.criterion: Contract tests pass for every operation that the RAES Go module delivers.
acceptance.evidence: No adapter or operation contract tests. Upstream #1825 is open; go-cutover contains tooling, not the required RAES application module.

acceptance.evidence: go.mod pins go1.27.3; go-check and CI build, vet and test.

acceptance.criterion: `verify` fails when the Go job fails.
acceptance.evidence: verify checks the Go job result and fails on non-success.

acceptance.criterion: The wheel and sdist contents do not change.
acceptance.evidence: PR #586 records unchanged wheel members, but the sdist gained ADR 0047. Literal unchanged contents were not met.

acceptance.criterion: `.gc/plan-rules.md` contains the release rule for Go-only pull requests.
acceptance.evidence: .gc/plan-rules.md requires non-releasing Go-only titles.

acceptance.criterion: A library package that prints, logs, reads the environment, or reads the clock fails CI.

issues.title: Go port 10: Port the pack filesystem boundary and the staged transactions
issues.evidence: Descriptor-based reads and Linux transactions exist. Audit fixes panic rollback and maximum read budget, and adds missing hardlink/byte fuzz coverage. Consumers outside packfs remain Python until their own chunks. Embedded collection support is still needed before cutover.

acceptance.criterion: Conformance cases and fuzz targets cover each rejection: symlink, hardlink, special file, non-canonical name, case-fold collision, escape, member budget, and byte budget.
acceptance.evidence: Rejection corpus exists. FuzzInventory lacked hardlink construction and no fuzzer exercised read byte budgets; audit adds both.

acceptance.criterion: Tests cover create, exchange, conflict, and recovery.
acceptance.evidence: Normal create/exchange/conflict/recovery tests exist. Audit adds panic rollback and failed panic-recovery tests.

acceptance.criterion: The lint, architecture, test, and mutation gates pass.
acceptance.evidence: Existing checks passed at the old head; new fixes require new checks.

issues.title: Go port 11: Port strict document ingest and full schema validation
issues.evidence: Standard full schema validator, strict decoder and shared Go secret policy exist. Audit fixes extreme-exponent panic and incorrect Unicode diagnostic. Python copies remain until consumers migrate. Rejection of ambiguous YAML values is a recorded deviation.

acceptance.criterion: Conformance cases show that a violation of each schema keyword fails with a stable code. The cases for `minLength` and the other keywords above are Python deviations.
acceptance.evidence: Unit tests cover packaged schema keywords. Command-level strict-schema cases await future Go consumers; Python skips name deviations.

acceptance.criterion: All hosted kit and pack documents pass.
acceptance.evidence: TestHostedDocuments checks the 140 hosted metadata documents. Must repeat after dev synchronization.

acceptance.criterion: Fuzz targets cover the decoder.
acceptance.evidence: JSON/YAML fuzzers exist. Audit adds extreme-exponent and Unicode regressions.

acceptance.criterion: One secret-shape policy exists, and no copy remains.
acceptance.evidence: One Go policy exists. Publication has a distinct documented rule. Python duplicates remain until their consumers migrate.

issues.title: Go port 12: Port the diagnostic model and the command outcome contract
issues.evidence: One product diagnostic, command outcome, terminal escaping and Python-compatible JSON writer exist. Developer findings and RAES transport diagnostics have distinct purposes. PR #618 fixes foreign absolute paths and usage escaping.

acceptance.criterion: One diagnostic type exists, and no package defines another.
acceptance.evidence: diagnostic owns product findings; report is developer output and raes.Diagnostic is transport data, not competing product policy.

acceptance.criterion: Conformance cases pass for exit codes, JSON-only stdout, and escaped terminal output for each command that exists when this chunk merges.
acceptance.evidence: Output helpers exist. #618 extends failure corpus and usage escaping. Future JSON commands must marshal before writing.

acceptance.criterion: Tests show that diagnostics carry no authored values and no absolute paths.
acceptance.evidence: Constructor and no-value tests exist; #618 rejects foreign absolute paths. Authored field names remain location data.
